title: The Lebesgue Integral and the Convergence Theorems

items.title: Extended-real-valued measurable functions
Nonnegative simple measurable functions
Closure properties of measurable functions used by the integral
items.strategy: Preimages of rays control sums and scalar multiples wherever the extended-real pointwise operations are defined. The same ray calculus handles positive and negative parts, products with indicators, countable infima, and monotone pointwise suprema.

items.title: Every nonnegative measurable function is the increasing limit of simple measurable functions
items.strategy: Use the dyadic truncations $2^{-n}\lfloor 2^n(f\wedge n)\rfloor$. They are simple, measurable, increase pointwise, and converge to $f$.

items.title: The integral of a nonnegative simple function
The simple integral is independent of the chosen representation
items.strategy: Refine two simple-function decompositions to a common measurable partition and compare the coefficient sums cell by cell. The $0\cdot\infty=0$ convention is consumed exactly when a zero coefficient multiplies an infinite-measure cell.

items.title: The simple integral is monotone, homogeneous, and additive
items.strategy: After a common refinement, additivity and homogeneity are coefficient algebra, and monotonicity is cellwise comparison of the refined coefficients.

items.title: The nonnegative Lebesgue integral
The nonnegative integral agrees with the simple integral on simple functions
items.strategy: A simple function is one of its own admissible simple minorants, and every competing minorant is bounded above by it coefficientwise.

items.title: Integral over a measurable subset
The indefinite integral of a nonnegative simple function is a measure
items.strategy: If $s=\sum c_j\chi_{E_j}$, then $A\mapsto\int_A s\,d\mu=\sum c_j\mu(A\cap E_j)$ is a finite nonnegative combination of measures.

items.title: Monotonicity and nonnegative homogeneity of the nonnegative integral
items.strategy: Monotonicity is immediate from the set of admissible simple minorants. For scaling, send simple minorants of $f$ to those of $cf$ and conversely.

items.title: Monotone convergence for the integral
items.strategy: The numbers $\int f_n$ increase and are bounded above by $\int f$. For the reverse inequality, fix simple $0\le s\le f$ and $c\in(0,1)$, use the simple-measure theorem on $A_n=\{f_n\ge cs\}$, and then let $c\uparrow1$.

items.title: Additivity of the nonnegative Lebesgue integral
items.strategy: Approximate the two summands from below by increasing simple sequences, add those sequences pointwise, and apply monotone convergence.

items.title: Beppo Levi's theorem for nonnegative series
items.strategy: Apply additivity to the partial sums $S_n=\sum_{k<n}f_k$ and then apply monotone convergence to $S_n\uparrow\sum_k f_k$.

items.title: The indefinite integral of a nonnegative measurable function is a measure
items.strategy: For $A_n\uparrow A$, apply monotone convergence to $f\chi_{A_n}$. The simple-case measure statement and additivity then upgrade $A\mapsto\int_A f\,d\mu$ to a measure.

items.title: The measure with density $f$ relative to $\mu$
Integrating against a density agrees with integrating the product
items.strategy: First prove the identity for simple $g$, where it is coefficient bookkeeping against the measure $\nu(A)=\int_A f\,d\mu$. Then pass to general $g\ge0$ by increasing simple approximation and monotone convergence.

items.title: Fatou's lemma
items.strategy: Apply monotone convergence to $g_n=\inf_{k\ge n}f_k$.

items.title: Reverse Fatou's lemma under an integrable majorant
items.strategy: Apply Fatou's lemma to the nonnegative functions $g-f_n$ and rearrange the resulting inequality.

items.title: A nonnegative measurable function has integral $0$ exactly when it vanishes almost everywhere
items.strategy: If $\int f=0$, then for $E_n=\{f\ge 1/n\}$ the inequality $(1/n)\chi_{E_n}\le f$ forces $\mu(E_n)=0$. The converse is immediate because every admissible simple minorant is supported on a null set.

items.title: A nonnegative measurable function with finite integral is finite almost everywhere
items.strategy: The set $\{f=\infty\}$ is contained in $\bigcap_n\{f\ge n\}$, and each of those sets has measure at most $n^{-1}\int f$.

items.title: A nonnegative integral over a null set vanishes
items.strategy: If $\mu(E)=0$, then every simple minorant of $f\chi_E$ integrates to $0$ because every coefficient is multiplied by a null set.

items.title: Almost-everywhere monotone convergence
items.strategy: Modify the sequence on the null exceptional set and use the null-set integral corollary to compare the original and modified integrals.

items.title: Chebyshev-Markov inequality for the integral
items.strategy: For $t>0$, the pointwise inequality $t\chi_{\{f\ge t\}}\le f$ integrates to the desired bound.

items.title: Integrable real and complex functions, and their integrals
The class $L^1(\mu)$ of integrable functions
The Lebesgue integral is linear on $L^1(\mu)$
items.strategy: For real functions, expand positive and negative parts and use nonnegative additivity. For complex functions, apply the real statement to the real and imaginary parts.

items.title: Two integrable functions are equal almost everywhere exactly when all of their indefinite integrals agree
items.strategy: If $f=g$ almost everywhere, then $(f-g)\chi_A$ vanishes almost everywhere for every measurable $A$, so every indefinite integral is $0$. Conversely, if $\int_A(f-g)\,d\mu=0$ for every measurable $A$, apply the nonnegative zero-integral criterion to $(f-g)^+$ and $(f-g)^-$.

items.title: The modulus of an integral is bounded by the integral of the modulus
items.strategy: For real $f$, use $-|f|\le f\le |f|$. For complex $f$, rotate by $\alpha=\overline{\int f}/|\int f|$ and compare $\Re(\alpha f)$ with $|f|$.

items.title: Dominated convergence
items.strategy: Use Fatou on the nonnegative functions $2g-|f_n-f|$ to obtain $L^1$ convergence. Linearity and the integral triangle inequality then give convergence of the integrals, and this route works for complex-valued functions as well as real-valued ones.

items.title: Bounded convergence on a finite measure space
items.strategy: Dominate the sequence by the constant bound times $\chi_X$ and apply dominated convergence.

items.title: Integrable simple functions are dense in $L^1(\mu)$
items.strategy: Approximate the positive and negative parts from below by simple functions and apply dominated convergence to the error terms.

items.title: Absolute continuity of the integral
items.strategy: Truncate $|f|$ by $|f|\wedge n$, use monotone convergence to control the tail, and bound the truncated part by $n\mu(E)$.

items.title: The indefinite integral of an integrable function is countably additive on measurable sets
items.strategy: Write $f=f^+-f^-$ and use the measure property of the two nonnegative indefinite integrals on disjoint unions.

items.title: Continuity under the integral sign
items.strategy: For any sequence $t_n\to t_0$, apply dominated convergence to $x\mapsto f(x,t_n)$ under the fixed dominator.

items.title: Differentiation under the integral sign
items.strategy: Apply dominated convergence to the difference quotients and use the mean value theorem, together with the dominating bound on $\partial_t f$, to control them uniformly on compact parameter intervals.

items.title: Jensen's integral inequality for a probability measure
items.strategy: Take a supporting line to $\varphi$ at $\int f\,d\mu$, integrate its inequality against the probability measure, and use the normalization $\mu(X)=1$.

items.title: FALSE: monotone convergence holds without monotonicity
items.strategy: Use the spike sequence $f_n=n\chi_{(0,1/n)}$ on $(0,1)$: it converges pointwise to $0$ but every integral is $1$.

items.title: FALSE: Fatou's lemma is always an equality
items.strategy: Use the travelling-mass sequence $f_n=\chi_{[n,n+1]}$ on $\mathbb R$: the liminf is $0$, while every integral is $1$.

items.title: FALSE: dominated convergence holds without a dominating function
items.strategy: Again take $f_n=n\chi_{(0,1/n)}$ on $(0,1)$; the pointwise limit is $0$ but the integrals stay equal to $1$.

items.title: FALSE: a nonnegative measurable function with integral $0$ vanishes everywhere
items.strategy: Use the Dirichlet function $\chi_{\mathbb Q\cap[0,1]}$, whose Lebesgue integral is $0$ although it is positive on a dense set.

items.title: FALSE: pointwise limits of integrable functions are integrable
items.strategy: On $(\mathbb N,\mathcal P(\mathbb N),\#)$, let $f_n=\chi_{\{1,\dots,n\}}$; each $f_n$ is integrable but the pointwise limit $1$ is not.

items.title: FALSE: the Lebesgue integral extends linearly to all measurable functions
items.strategy: On $\mathbb R$ with Lebesgue measure, take $f=\chi_{[0,\infty)}$ and $g=-\chi_{[0,\infty)}$; then $f+g=0$ is integrable although neither summand is, so no linear extension can assign values to all three consistently.

items.title: FALSE: Jensen's inequality holds on an infinite measure space without normalization
items.strategy: On $(\mathbb N,\mathcal P(\mathbb N),\#)$, take $f=\chi_{\{1,2\}}$ and $\varphi(x)=x^2$; then $\varphi(\int f)=4>2=\int\varphi(f)$.

title: The Lebesgue Integral and the Convergence Theorems — Examples

items.title: Integrating against counting measure recovers a series
items.strategy: Write the function as the increasing limit of its finite-support truncations and identify each truncated integral with the corresponding finite sum.

items.title: The Dirichlet function is positive on a dense set but has Lebesgue integral $0$
items.strategy: Its support is the countable set $\mathbb Q\cap[0,1]$, so the whole integral lives on a null set even though the function is positive at every rational point.

items.title: The exponential tail function is integrable by monotone truncation and geometric comparison
items.strategy: Approximate by $f_n=e^{-x}\chi_{[0,n]}$. On each interval $[k,k+1]$, one has $e^{-x}\le e^{-k}$, so interval measures and the geometric series bound the tails while monotone convergence identifies the limit.

items.title: The function $x^{-1/2}$ on $(0,1]$ is unbounded and integrable
items.strategy: Use the truncations $f_n(x)=\min\{x^{-1/2},n\}$. On the dyadic interval $(2^{-(k+1)},2^{-k}]$, one has $x^{-1/2}\le 2^{(k+1)/2}$, so the interval measure gives a convergent geometric bound on the total integral.

items.title: Integrating against a Dirac measure is evaluation at the point
items.strategy: Start from simple functions, where only the coefficient of the atom at $x_0$ survives, and then pass to general nonnegative and integrable functions.

items.title: Differentiating $\int_0^{\infty} e^{-tx}\sin x\,dx$ under the integral sign
items.strategy: Use the dominating function $xe^{-ax}$ on any compact parameter interval $[a,b]\subset(0,\infty)$ and differentiate under the integral sign. The resulting parameter integral is the standard starting point for the later closed-form evaluation, but the example's point here is the legal differentiation step itself.

items.title: Jensen's inequality yields the weighted AM-GM inequality
items.strategy: Apply Jensen to the convex function $\varphi(x)=-\log x$ on $(0,\infty)$ over a finite discrete probability space.

items.title: Fatou can be strict and domination can fail simultaneously
items.strategy: Use the spike sequence $f_n=n\chi_{(0,1/n)}$ on $(0,1)$: the pointwise limit is $0$, the liminf integral is $0$, and every integral is $1$.

items.title: A pointwise limit of integrable functions need not be integrable
items.strategy: On counting measure, the indicators of the initial segments $\{1,\dots,n\}$ converge pointwise to the constant function $1$, which has infinite integral.

items.title: Mass can escape to infinity under pointwise convergence
items.strategy: The travelling indicators $\chi_{[n,n+1]}$ converge pointwise to $0$ on $\mathbb R$, but every integral stays equal to $1$.

items.title: Uniform convergence does not force convergence of integrals on an infinite-measure space
items.strategy: The functions $f_n=n^{-1}\chi_{[0,n]}$ converge uniformly to $0$ on $\mathbb R$, but every integral is $1$.

items.title: A decreasing sequence need not satisfy a monotone convergence theorem without an integrable start
items.strategy: The indicators $\chi_{[n,\infty)}$ decrease pointwise to $0$ on $\mathbb R$, but each integral is infinite.

items.title: Linearity can fail without an integrability hypothesis
items.strategy: Take $f=\chi_{[0,\infty)}$ and $g=-\chi_{[0,\infty)}$ on $\mathbb R$; then $f+g=0$ is integrable although neither $f$ nor $g$ is.

items.title: Jensen's inequality can fail on an infinite measure space without normalization
items.strategy: On counting measure over $\mathbb N$, let $f=\chi_{\{1,2\}}$ and $\varphi(x)=x^2$; then $\varphi(\int f)=4$ while $\int\varphi(f)=2$.
